messages.subject: Fwd: GSoC 2018: R project for statistical computing has been accepted as a mentor organization!
messages.subject_clean: GSoC 2018: R project for statistical computing has been accepted as a mentor organization!
messages.body_plain:
R has been accepted by Google to be a GSoC mentoring organization again in 2018!

Now the work for everyone else in the organization picks up.

Potential mentors: if you haven't already done so, please polish your project idea pages on the wiki here:

https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2018/wiki/table%20of%20proposed%20coding%20projects

Project idea pages are a non-optional part of the process, required both by Google and by R GSoC policies.  These projects are competitive, and are chosen based on all of the material prov ided by students and by mentors.

Potential students: now is the time to start contacting mentors for posted ideas, providing patches, submitting test results, etc. to really show your interest in working on an R GSoC project in 2018.  You can even start working on your project application.  The best and most successful student applications typically run to about 10 pages if printed, so it is hard to write the entire thing in the space of the application period.  Expect more idea pages to be posted or finished over the next week or two.

If you have questions, please direct them to the list if they are general, or to Toby or me if they need to be handled privately.

Regards,

Brian

messages.subject: Mentors needed for Optimal Control Project
messages.subject_clean: Mentors needed for Optimal Control Project
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am proposing the project: Optimal Control for this summer.
Last year a Control Systems Toolbox  <https://github.com/benubah/control/>was released as part of GSoC 2017 and the CVXR  <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/CVXR/index.html>optimization package
also appeared on CRAN last year.
For this year, I am proposing on using the CVXR modeling package to provide optimal control functionality
for the R Community. Generally, bringing optimization to parts of  control systems.
MATLAB and Python have tools for this purpose, but this is not available in R yet.

Optimal Control has a wide range of applications in life sciences, systems biology, finance, engineering,
supply chain management, aerospace studies, missile systems, etc. See a good list of some application areas and
samples from PROPT in MATLAB: http://tomdyn.com/matlab_optimal_control_examples.html

The idea page is here: https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2018/wiki/Optimal-Control

So, I'm looking out for interested mentors.

Thank you

Best,
Ben Ubah
